json.title: perf(chart-data): ensure_totals_available re-runs percent-metric totals query on every request, bypassing QueryCacheManager (INC-B1081392)

labels.name: incident-autopilot
labels.description: Created by the incident triage automation

labels.name: autopilot-managed
labels.description: Admit this issue to the Devin remediation control plane

json.body:
<!-- devin-autopilot-run:INC-B1081392 -->

**Incident:** `datadog:incident:a75a6a38-caeb-4c08-b0bf-a9a81571b545` (SEV-3, service `luma-embedded-analytics`, scenario CD-1)
**Attribution confidence:** 0.8 (agent report) — independently confirmed by code inspection at `4511c13` (see "Confirmation" below).

## Customer impact
Embedded table charts that use percent metrics with `percent_metric_calculation = 'all_records'` intermittently exceed the host app's 5 s render budget under multi-tenant load. Signals at trigger: chart timeout rate 18.7% (threshold 5%), p95 chart latency 6320 ms, 14 tenants affected. Other chart types (`big_number_total`, `echarts_timeseries_line`) on the same dashboards/tenants had 0 timeouts.

## Observed behavior
On every synchronous `POST /api/v1/chart/data` for such a table, the "totals" query (`SELECT SUM(revenue) FROM orders WHERE tenant_id=? AND order_ts ...`, no GROUP BY, full scan) is executed against the warehouse **even when the whole payload is cache-warm**. Warehouse digest: totals fingerprint ran 164× vs 21 baseline — exactly the number of 200-status chart-data requests — while the grouped query ran only 9× (served from cache). APM traces show `cache_metadata='loaded'`, `superset_status=200`, yet 6.4–7.3 s duration.

## Expected behavior
The totals query should run at most once and be served from `QueryCacheManager` (DATA region) thereafter, like the main query. A cache-warm chart-data request should issue zero warehouse queries.

## Root cause / likely code area
`QueryContextProcessor.get_payload_result()` (`superset/common/query_context_processor.py` ~L646-684) calls `ensure_totals_available()` on every non-`force_cached` request. `ensure_totals_available()` (~L605-631) does:

```python
totals_query = self._query_context.queries[totals_idx]
result = self._query_context.get_query_result(totals_query)   # <- uncached
```

`QueryContext.get_query_result` → `QueryContextProcessor.get_query_result` → `self._qc_datasource.get_query_result(query_object)` → `ExploreMixin.get_query_result()` (`superset/models/helpers.py` ~L2604) → `self.query(...)`. There is no `QueryCacheManager` lookup anywhere on this path. Afterwards the same totals query object is also processed by `get_query_results_with_timing` (cached path), so on a warm cache the totals SQL still hits the warehouse once per request.

Contrast: the async path `superset/tasks/async_queries.py::_inject_contribution_totals` (~L170-202) explicitly reads the totals dataframe from `QueryCacheManager.get(key=..., region=CacheRegion.DATA)` instead of re-running it — the intended behaviour the sync path lacks.

The extra columns-less totals query is emitted by `superset-frontend/plugins/plugin-chart-table/src/buildQuery.ts` (~L334-351) when `percent_metric_calculation === 'all_records'`; `normalize_contribution_totals()` selects it as `totals_idx`.

## Reproduction steps
1. Create a Table chart with a metric and at least one **percent metric** (e.g. `SUM(revenue)`), set *Percent metric calculation* = **All records**, and group by a dimension on a moderately large dataset.
2. Enable data caching (`DATA_CACHE_CONFIG`) and load the chart twice.
3. Observe warehouse query log / `db_engine` logs: the no-GROUP-BY `SELECT SUM(revenue) ...` query executes on **both** loads, while the grouped query executes only on the first.
4. Unit-level: build a `QueryContextProcessor` with two queries (grouped + totals with `columns=[]`), warm the DATA cache for both, mock the datasource `query`/`get_query_result`, call `get_payload_result()` → datasource is still queried once (totals). Existing tests `tests/unit_tests/common/test_query_context_processor.py::test_ensure_totals_available_updates_cache_values` show the mocking setup.

## Evidence
- RUM: all 36 timeouts are `table_v2` charts (112 views, p95 6810 ms); other viz types 0 timeouts.
- Every timed-out chart has `percent_metrics=[SUM(revenue)]` + `percent_metric_calculation='all_records'`; the one `row_limit` table is not among the timeouts.
- Warehouse: totals fingerprint 164× vs 21 baseline (p95 2140 ms, 100k rows scanned); grouped fingerprint 9× vs 12 baseline.
- Edge gateway 499s rose only on the chart-data route (client aborts on slow-but-successful responses).
- No deploys in the incident window; HEAD `4511c13` is a psycopg2-binary bump only. Latent defect from the original `all_records` feature (#33656) surfacing under load.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `ensure_totals_available()` obtains the totals dataframe through the cached path (`get_df_payload_result` / `QueryCacheManager` lookup, mirroring `_inject_contribution_totals`) so the totals SQL executes at most once per cache TTL.
- [ ] A cache-warm `get_payload_result()` for an `all_records` percent-metric table issues no datasource query (new unit test in `tests/unit_tests/common/test_query_context_processor.py` asserting the datasource is not queried when the totals cache entry is loaded).
- [ ] Existing tests `test_ensure_totals_available_updates_cache_values` and `test_cache_values_sync_after_ensure_totals_available` still pass; cache keys are unaffected (`contribution_totals` remains stripped from the key).
- [ ] `force_cached=True` behaviour unchanged.

## Related-component context (not owners of the defect)
- `engineerA314/devin-demo` (embedded-analytics-product / luma-web): owns the 5000 ms render budget that converts slow 200 responses into RUM timeouts and 499s; surfaces the symptom only.
- `data-platform/warehouse-config` (analytics-warehouse): healthy; queue depth rose purely from the redundant totals query volume. Missing aggregation/indexing for the 100k-row scan is a contributing factor, and `percent_metric_calculation='row_limit'` or a higher render budget would mitigate the symptom without fixing the redundant query.

## Confirmation notes / caveats
- Confirmed by static inspection of the code path above at `4511c13`; no runtime reproduction was possible in this environment (no Python venv / pytest for the backend).
- p50 chart-data latency of ~1.36 s indicates the grouped query is itself non-trivial; the totals query is the dominant but not sole contributor.
